chrome-devtools.description: ADR-0038 (Issues #174, #224, #220 D7). A browser for product-lead's read-only sweep, bounded by origin. Since #224 it always attaches to the owner's own running Chrome (--autoConnect, the stable channel's default profile), so it drives a browser holding his logins and Chrome asks him to allow the connection, in any project whose agent calls it. The shell reads HARNESS_SWEEP_ORIGIN when the server starts, from the environment the harness gives it, which carries the project's settings env. Since #220 (D7) the value is a list of origins separated by single spaces, and each one becomes its own --allowedUrlPattern. Each must begin http:// or https:// and have a host of plain letters, digits, dots and hyphens with an optional :port. If the value is empty, carries any control character (a tab or a newline included), has an empty element (a leading, trailing or doubled space) or any element fails, the whole list is replaced by the discard port, so the browser reaches nothing. The package is pinned to one exact version and fetched with install scripts off.
args: o=$HARNESS_SWEEP_ORIGIN; ok=1; [ "$(printf '%s' "$o" | tr -d '\000-\037\177')" = "$o" ] || ok=0; case "$o" in ''|' '*|*' '|*'  '*) ok=0 ;; esac; set -f; IFS=' '; set -- $o; unset IFS; for u in "$@"; do case "$u" in http://*|https://*) ;; *) ok=0 ;; esac; h=$(printf '%s' "$u" | cut -d/ -f3); case "$h" in ''|*[!abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyzABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789.:-]*|:*|*:|*:*[!0123456789]*) ok=0 ;; esac; done; [ "$ok" = 1 ] || { o='http://127.0.0.1:9/*'; set -- "$o"; }; n=$#; for u in "$@"; do set -- "$@" --allowedUrlPattern "$u"; done; shift "$n"; exec npx --ignore-scripts -y chrome-devtools-mcp@1.8.0 --autoConnect --channel stable --no-usage-statistics --no-performance-crux "$@"
